prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro CBTC: separation, movement authority (MA), regulation. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (LTC): selects hold/skip-stop/turnback/run-through, confirms after Lantern shows it; produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice; no vital intervention; station holds via dispatch controls feed CBTC departure logic, route locking unchanged. Revenue Train Operator: sees MA, speed, location confidence; acknowledges to Atlas (stale rejected); repeats back voice instructions; departure blocked until door state compatible. Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple: records track clearance before restoring routes. Cyber Security Officer: reviews certificates, access, authentication failures before renewed config, and passenger-info/dispatch workstation access at commissioning or change. Elements: Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern: regulation; sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas; shows routes, points, occupancy, station/platform states using workstation identifiers; coordinates timetable deviation, platform closure, crowding before passenger release. North District Zone Controller, alias Marble (East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon) and South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid (West Junction Interlocking): send MA to Atlas; handover after odometer and receiving-zone validation; Marble suppresses departure on unsafe door state. Interlockings keep vital authority and overlap/flank protection; lost point correspondence shortens or withdraws MA. Falcon: Axle Counter Reset Request, inhibited if locked/approaching. West Junction: Route Release Exception List, route states. Platform Screen Door Controller: Platform Door Status Snapshot per face to CBTC. Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel: validates token, enforces MA, produces Brake Curve Checksum Log, reports door side, berth, departure readiness; modes initialization, protected manual, ATO, fallback, cutout; radio loss keeps last MA. Dual Channel Odometer. Train Radio Modem uses Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack before renewed sessions, via Wayside Radio Access Network, alias Saffron (Radio Handover Audit File). Safety Data Communication Network separates safety from passenger traffic; sends Clock Drift Sample Report to Cryptographic Key Management Appliance, which makes the Renewal Pack. Maintenance Diagnostic Server, alias Quarry: trends, interface faults, rejected commands to Maple. Service Timetable Server: planned context. Passenger Information Gateway gets reconciled predictions and platform data; no destination/skip-stop change until identity and route confirmed. Station staff states from validated CBTC data. Voice Dispatch Console shows identity, platform, hold reason; cancelled hold distinct from timeout/failure/rejection.

New part:
S150: During degraded operation, the CBTC system favours restrictive platform states and requires explicit controller action before restoring automatic departure support at the affected station.
S151: Diagnostics and maintenance for the Greenvale Metro communications-based train control system are organised around prompt event collection, controlled remote access, and traceable engineering decisions.
S152: Each safety-related part records time-stamped events for state changes, command acceptance, rejected commands, communication loss, and local protective actions.
S153: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server receives event streams from fixed and onboard equipment through monitored interfaces that do not allow maintenance traffic to alter train movement authority.
S154: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server uses the checksum log to compare stored braking data identifiers against the expected maintenance baseline for the affected train.
S155: Remote diagnostic sessions are initiated by a Signal Maintenance Engineer and are limited to read-only observation unless an approved maintenance window authorises a specific intervention.
S156: The Cyber Security Officer reviews privileged diagnostic access logs and confirms that remote connections use current credentials and approved encryption settings.
S157: The Line Traffic Controller receives the Route Release Exception List during incident triage and uses it to check whether a release anomaly could affect service recovery decisions.
S158: Marble records controller health, interface state, and fallback mode transitions in a form that can be correlated with adjacent wayside and operations records.
S159: The South District Zone Controller maintains comparable diagnostic coverage so that boundary events can be reviewed without relying on a single source of evidence.
S160: The East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking report route command histories, point detection changes, and protective lock status to support failure localisation.
S161: The Atlas Onboard Controller stores onboard fault codes, movement authority acceptance records, propulsion cutback requests, and train interface exceptions for later retrieval.
S162: The Dual Channel Odometer provides distance and speed plausibility information that is retained with trainborne diagnostic records after any odometry disagreement.
S163: The Train Radio Modem records bearer loss, reconnection timing, signal quality indicators, and message retry counts needed to distinguish radio coverage issues from equipment faults.
S164: The Wayside Radio Access Network and Safety Data Communication Network provide communication performance records that are compared with controller logs during network-related investigations.
S165: The Metro Operations Control System displays selected fault summaries to the Line Traffic Controller but does not expose detailed maintenance commands at the traffic control workstation.
S166: A Revenue Train Operator reports observed cab indications, train handling effects, and passenger service impacts using the operational reporting channel defined for degraded service.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
